description: Expected outcomes for the bundled synthetic scenarios. Used by `attackpath validate` and the regression test suite. Every fixture is synthetic; see docs/incident-scenarios.md for the narrative behind each one.

scenarios.name: 01-overly-broad-role
scenarios.description: A role with Action * on Resource * is reported as administrative.

expect.note: administrative access already implies the wildcard grant

scenarios.name: 02-risky-trust
scenarios.description: Anonymous trust, cross-account trust without ExternalId, and cross-account trust with ExternalId.

expect.note: any AWS principal -> vendor-support-access -> PII bucket
the sts:ExternalId condition value is request-time context

scenarios.name: 03-passrole-broad
scenarios.description: A deployment user holds iam:PassRole on * together with Lambda write permissions.

scenarios.name: 04-workload-s3-access
scenarios.description: A function's execution role has S3 full access and therefore reaches a high-sensitivity bucket.

expect.note: function -> own role -> bucket is the same fact as the workload finding

scenarios.name: 05-public-bucket
scenarios.description: Public bucket policies: effective, mitigated by Block Public Access, and intentionally public low-sensitivity data.

scenarios.name: 06-explicit-deny
scenarios.description: A group grants s3:GetObject on * but an inline Deny blocks the PII bucket; the deny must win.

expect.note: explicit Deny on the PII bucket

scenarios.name: 07-unknown-condition
scenarios.description: An Allow guarded by aws:SourceVpce cannot be decided offline and is reported as indeterminate.

scenarios.name: 08-safe-configuration
scenarios.description: A least-privilege execution role scoped to its two buckets produces no high-severity finding.

scenarios.name: 09-incomplete-inventory
scenarios.description: Unresolved managed policy, missing execution role and partial Lambda coverage produce coverage warnings.

expect.note: a missing document alone must not produce a privilege finding

scenarios.name: 10-remediation-before
scenarios.description: A user with sts:AssumeRole on * reaches an administrative role trusted by the whole account.

scenarios.name: 10-remediation-after
scenarios.description: The same environment after scoping sts:AssumeRole and narrowing the trust policy: the path is gone.

expect.note: the role itself is still administrative; only the path to it was removed

scenarios.name: 11-public-instance-path
scenarios.description: An internet-exposed jump host runs with a role that reads the PII bucket (a multi-service path), a web instance exposes SSH and allows IMDSv1, and a private worker produces no exposure finding.

expect.note: every port open to the internet on a host whose role reads PII
the internet -> jump host -> instance role -> PII bucket; capped at high because the first hop assumes a compromise
SSH is open to the internet next to the web ports
private subnet and no public address
IMDSv2 is required on the worker
instance -> own role -> bucket is the workload fact SENSITIVE-ACCESS reports
